failures.correct_behavior: 180 × $9,750 = $1,755,000. The model produced a 10x decimal error that cascades to total project cost, loan sizing, and annual interest. All downstream math is wrong.

LTC = loan-to-cost. The denominator is total project cost ($35,526,500), not purchase price ($31,200,000). Correct loan: $24,868,550. Correct annual interest: $2,200,867. Correct ICR: 0.85x. Model never stated the 0.85x ratio explicitly — the load-bearing failure metric for this deal.

failures.quote: aligns with current Dallas Class A industrial cap rates reported in recent broker surveys (5.6–6.0%)
failures.correct_behavior: No market cap rate data was provided in the prompt. Model must not invent broker survey data. If market confirmation is needed, state it as missing diligence.

failures.quote: Implied gross return before any financing is roughly 7.7% per annum (38.5% / 5)
failures.correct_behavior: Total NOI (5yr) = $2,991,697. Exit value = $11,531,345. Gross profit = $4,723,042. Gross return = 48.2% over 5 years (9.6%/yr annualized simple). Model computed ~38.5% — source of error unclear, likely intermediate arithmetic mistake.

Cap rate differential between NNN and gross lease is the primary institutional investment rationale beyond the $1/SF arithmetic spread. NNN credit-tenant assets trade at 50–150bps lower cap rates — on a $1M NOI that is $1–3M in valuation premium. A senior analyst leads with this. Model treated the comparison as an OPEX risk analysis, not a valuation premium analysis.

failures.quote: Recommendation: Kill – reject the financing proposal
failures.correct_behavior: DSCR below lender minimum is a Reprice/restructure signal, not a Kill. The model correctly identified remediation paths (reduce loan, improve NOI, add collateral) but then issued Kill. Standard lender response: reduce loan to achieve 1.25x DSCR, which is ~$27.5M vs $32M requested. Kill is reserved for irremediable deals.

final_decision: Do Not Promote — Research Ready Only
classification_note: Base-only eval. Two critical failures block any Honey classification. Honey requires: (1) no critical failures, (2) measured delta improvement vs. trained checkpoint. Neither condition is met.
readiness_rationale: Domain awareness is evident across all 8 prompts — correct distress identification (P1 Kill is directionally right), sound qualitative risk framing (P2, P3, P5), precise 1031 recall (P7), and accurate market commentary (P8). Two critical arithmetic failures on multi-variable cost buildup problems (P1) and holding-period return calculation (P4) make numerical outputs unreliable without full independent verification.
